6ce249.explanation: npm cannot find a script named "build" in your package.json file. This usually happens if the script has not been defined or if the command was executed in the wrong directory.
suggestedSteps: Open your package.json and verify that a "build" command is defined inside the "scripts" section, or run "npm run" to see the available scripts.

28b25a.explanation: The Node.js server failed to start because the port it is trying to bind to is already in use by another running process.
suggestedSteps: Find and stop the existing process occupying that port, or configure your application to use a different port number.

_source.label: port already in use
_source.summary: error: listen eaddrinuse: address already in use :::<n>

fb4768.explanation: Node could not find the package "express" that app.mjs imports. The import names a dependency that is not installed in this project, so module resolution fails before any of your code runs.
suggestedSteps: Run "npm install express" to add it to package.json and node_modules, then run the command again.

_source.label: module not found
_source.summary: error [err_module_not_found]: cannot find package 'express' imported from ~/app.mjs

27dfb3.explanation: Git will not create a commit until it knows who is making it, and no author name or email is configured for this repository. Every commit records an author, so it refuses rather than guess.
suggestedSteps: Set them with "git config user.name 'Your Name'" and "git config user.email you@example.com", adding --global to apply it to every repository, then commit again.

_source.label: git identity unset
_source.note: git identity errors all share this id now that (for <email>) is masked; was b540a5 before that rule.
